title: Power Automate: debug desktop flows using variable default values
summary: The briefing passes: its maker controls, local desktop-flow licensing and roadmap details are supported. Microsoft documents the warning about sensitive input defaults and their storage, while searches found no dedicated administrator switch or default-value API.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Makers can define flow-variable defaults in the desktop flow designer and start execution at a selected action using them.
claims.quote: Start execution from a selected action using the variables' default values (Run from here with default values).

claims.claim: Learn describes testing different scenarios without modifying actions or restarting the flow from the beginning.
claims.quote: These capabilities help you test different scenarios without modifying actions or restarting the flow from the beginning.

claims.claim: The maker path is Power Automate for desktop: Variables pane > flow variable > Edit flow variable > Default value.
claims.quote:
Double-click a flow variable (or use its menu) to open **Edit flow variable**.
**Default value**: The value applied when running the flow with default values.

claims.claim: The Edit flow variable dialog lets makers set a default data type.
claims.quote: **Default data type**: The type used for the default value.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Right-clicking an action offers Run from here with default values, with shortcut Alt+F5.
claims.quote:
Right-click the action you want to start from.
- Select **Run from here with default values** (Alt+F5).

claims.claim: The separate Run from here command starts at the selected action and ignores previous actions.
claims.quote: To run the flow starting from a specific action, right-click the action and select **Run from here**. This ignores all previous actions and runs the flow from the selected action onwards.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the feature is enabled automatically for admins, makers and marketers.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Defaults of sensitive input variables are not protected in action modals or the flow definition in Dataverse.
claims.quote: The default values aren't protected in the action modals and the flow definition in Dataverse.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: For desktop flows saved using v2 schema, variable default values contribute to the stored Dataverse flow definition.
claims.quote: The limit applies to the definition of the desktop flow saved in Dataverse, which can't exceed 16M characters. The issue can occur with a large desktop flow, such as when actions have large property values or variables have large default values.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Marking a flow variable as sensitive is a separate maker setting that masks its value in the designer UI.
claims.quote: **Mark as sensitive**: Masks the variable value in the UI.

claims.claim: Learn describes sensitive-variable masking during debugging as basic protection against screen observers.
claims.quote: Masking sensitive variables during debugging provides only a basic form of protection to developers from third parties looking at their screens.

claims.claim: Existing desktop-flow sharing governs collaborators' ability to open and edit a flow.
claims.quote: To enable other makers to manage your flow and collaborate on it, share it with them with **Co-owner access**.

claims.claim: A Learn debugging walkthrough tells makers to delete default values before leaving the authoring experience.
claims.quote: Delete all default values before you leave the desktop flow authoring experience in Power Automate Desktop.

claims.claim: The feature page lists a known issue that flows built or edited with version 2.14 or later cannot be opened or run with older versions.
claims.quote: Flows built or edited with Power Automate for desktop version 2.14 or above are incompatible with older versions of Power Automate for desktop. You can't use older versions of Power Automate for desktop to open or run these flows.
